draft.title: Inner Game Readiness Assessment for Founders and Creators
draft.question: How well does the respondent recognize and address the psychological bottlenecks (fear, identity, self-sabotage) that limit their business growth, as framed by Corey Wilks' approach?

dimensions.name: Pattern Recognition
dimensions.note: Ability to identify underlying psychological patterns beneath surface-level business problems.
observable_manifestations: When facing a business challenge, respondent looks for recurring emotional or behavioral patterns in themselves.
Respondent can articulate how a specific fear (e.g., fear of judgment) manifests in their work habits.
Respondent distinguishes between surface productivity issues and deeper identity-level blocks.
Respondent uses language like 'pattern', 'fear', 'identity' when describing setbacks.
Respondent can connect past experiences to current business decisions.
evidence: Testimonial: 'I'd come in with a business question and leave understanding the pattern in me that created it.'
Article: 'The Action Gap – 9 reasons even the most ambitious people struggle to achieve what they're capable of…'
Article: 'Why Ambitious People Sabotage Their Success – Hint: It's not because you lack discipline…'

dimensions.name: Fear Engagement
dimensions.note: Willingness to confront and transform fear rather than avoid or suppress it.
observable_manifestations: Respondent can name specific fears (e.g., imposter syndrome, perfectionism) that affect their work.
Respondent has tried strategies to work with fear (e.g., exposure, reframing) rather than just pushing through.
Respondent views fear as a potential catalyst for growth, not just an obstacle.
Respondent can describe a time they acted despite fear and what they learned.
Respondent seeks resources or frameworks (like the Four Horsemen of Fear) to understand their fears.
evidence: Program description: 'transform your relationship with fear so it becomes a catalyst for growth instead of an obstacle'
Testimonial: 'His Four Horsemen of Fear framework completely transformed the way I operate in my life and business.'
Article: 'The Four Horsemen of Fear – A deep dive into the most common limiting beliefs holding you back.'

dimensions.name: Self-Awareness Depth
dimensions.note: Capacity for introspection and recognizing identity-level factors that influence behavior.
observable_manifestations: Respondent can articulate how their self-concept (e.g., 'I'm not a salesperson') affects their choices.
Respondent reflects on existential questions about purpose and meaning in their work.
Respondent can identify moments when they self-sabotage and the underlying beliefs driving that.
Respondent is open to feedback that challenges their self-perception.
Respondent regularly engages in reflective practices (journaling, therapy, coaching).
evidence: Site description: 'the deeply psychological, existential, and identity-level aspects still capping your potential.'
Article: 'Liminal Tension: A New Way to Think About Imposter Syndrome – What if Imposter Syndrome wasn't a sign to back off, but actually a good sign?'
Article: 'How to Get Ahead of 99% of People – A non-hyperbolic, psychology-based understanding of what holds us back from self-actualization'

dimensions.name: Action Orientation
dimensions.note: Tendency to translate insights into concrete behavioral changes and consistent action.
observable_manifestations: Respondent sets specific goals based on their psychological insights.
Respondent experiments with new behaviors (e.g., publishing despite fear) and tracks outcomes.
Respondent can describe a recent change they made after recognizing a pattern.
Respondent follows through on commitments to themselves (e.g., daily practices).
Respondent seeks accountability (coach, peer group) to maintain momentum.
evidence: Testimonial: 'it's changed how I lead, how I make decisions, and honestly, how I live.'
Testimonial: 'he goes deeper into understanding the fears that prevent us from publishing and iterating.'
Article: 'How to Change Your Life (Starting Today) – Evolution is a requirement for success.'

dimensions.name: Openness to Psychological Work
dimensions.note: Receptivity to exploring emotional and identity-level issues as part of professional development.
observable_manifestations: Respondent is willing to discuss feelings, fears, and personal history in a coaching context.
Respondent values psychological insights over quick-fix productivity hacks.
Respondent has invested in therapy, coaching, or self-development programs.
Respondent is comfortable with vulnerability and uncertainty in personal exploration.
Respondent seeks out content (books, podcasts) on psychology and personal growth.
evidence: Site positioning: 'psychologist turned coach' and 'inner game' focus.
Testimonial: 'He doesn't just address surface-level productivity tips; he goes deeper.'
Newsletter: 'Creator Alchemy newsletter to get insights designed to help you remove the psychological bottlenecks.'

dimensions.name: Integration of Feedback
dimensions.note: Ability to use external feedback to uncover blind spots and adjust behavior.
observable_manifestations: Respondent actively seeks feedback from peers, mentors, or coaches.
Respondent can recall a specific piece of feedback that led to a behavioral change.
Respondent does not become defensive when feedback challenges their self-image.
Respondent asks clarifying questions to understand the root of feedback.
Respondent follows up on feedback with action plans.
evidence: Testimonial: 'Corey has the skill to consistently get underneath the surface problem to the real one.'
Coaching service: 'Ongoing coaching to dive deep into what's holding you back, what you actually want, and how to achieve it.'
Testimonial: 'I'd come in with a business question and leave understanding the pattern in me that created it.'

questions.text: You're about to launch a new product, but you keep delaying the final steps. Which of the following best describes your internal experience?
questions.what_it_tests: Ability to recognize fear-based patterns like perfectionism or imposter syndrome.
questions.scoring_logic: High: Respondent identifies a specific fear (e.g., fear of judgment) and connects it to the delay. Medium: Mentions general anxiety or stress. Low: Attributes delay to external factors or lack of discipline.
questions.strong_signal: Says something like 'I realize I'm afraid of criticism, so I keep tweaking to avoid judgment.'
questions.weak_signal: Says 'I just need to manage my time better.'
source_basis: Article: 'The Four Horsemen of Fear'
Testimonial: 'fears that prevent us from publishing and iterating.'

questions.text: A client gives you feedback that your work feels 'too safe.' Your immediate reaction is to...
questions.what_it_tests: Openness to feedback and ability to see it as information about patterns, not personal attack.
questions.scoring_logic: High: Respondent reflects on the feedback, asks questions, and considers how fear of risk might be showing up. Medium: Feels defensive but eventually considers it. Low: Dismisses feedback or takes it personally without reflection.
questions.strong_signal: Says 'I'd ask them for examples and then reflect on whether I'm avoiding risk due to fear of failure.'
questions.weak_signal: Says 'I'd ignore it because they don't know my process.'
confounders: Emotional state at time of feedback
source_basis: Testimonial: 'get underneath the surface problem to the real one.'
Coaching service: 'dive deep into what's holding you back.'

questions.text: When you think about your biggest business challenge right now, which of the following feels most true?
questions.what_it_tests: Ability to identify underlying psychological patterns versus surface-level issues.
questions.scoring_logic: High: Respondent names a recurring pattern (e.g., 'I always procrastinate when I need to ask for money'). Medium: Describes a specific problem without connecting to a pattern. Low: Blames external circumstances or lacks insight.
questions.strong_signal: Says 'I notice I consistently avoid sales conversations because I fear rejection, which stems from a belief that I'm not good enough.'
questions.weak_signal: Says 'My challenge is I don't have enough time.'
source_basis: Article: 'The Action Gap'
Testimonial: 'leave understanding the pattern in me that created it.'

questions.text: You've been feeling stuck in your business for months. A coach suggests exploring your identity and fears. How do you respond?
questions.what_it_tests: Receptivity to psychological and identity-level exploration as part of professional growth.
questions.scoring_logic: High: Respondent is curious and willing to engage. Medium: Hesitant but open to trying. Low: Rejects the idea as 'too touchy-feely' or irrelevant.
questions.strong_signal: Says 'I'm open to it because I suspect there's something deeper going on.'
questions.weak_signal: Says 'I'd rather focus on concrete strategies.'
source_basis: Site positioning: 'psychologist turned coach'
Testimonial: 'He doesn't just address surface-level productivity tips.'

questions.text: After a coaching session, you identify a fear of being seen as 'not an expert.' What do you do next?
questions.what_it_tests: Tendency to translate psychological insights into concrete actions.
questions.scoring_logic: High: Respondent describes a specific behavioral experiment (e.g., publishing a post despite fear). Medium: Plans to think about it more. Low: Does nothing or forgets.
questions.strong_signal: Says 'I'll write and publish a piece that challenges that belief, even if it's uncomfortable.'
source_basis: Testimonial: 'changed how I lead, how I make decisions'
Article: 'How to Change Your Life (Starting Today)'

questions.text: Which of the following best describes your approach to personal development?
questions.what_it_tests: Preference for psychological depth versus surface-level tactics.
questions.behavior_being_tested: Openness to psychological work and self-awareness depth.
questions.scoring_logic: High: Chooses options emphasizing understanding root causes and identity. Medium: Balanced approach. Low: Prefers quick fixes and productivity hacks.
questions.strong_signal: Selects 'I want to understand the deeper patterns driving my behavior.'
questions.weak_signal: Selects 'I want actionable tips I can implement immediately.'
source_basis: Site description: 'deeply psychological, existential, and identity-level aspects'
Testimonial: 'He doesn't just address surface-level productivity tips.'

recommended_interventions: For low Pattern Recognition: Introduce the Four Horsemen of Fear framework and ask client to map recent business challenges to each fear.
For low Fear Engagement: Use exposure-based exercises to help client approach feared situations gradually.
For low Self-Awareness Depth: Encourage journaling prompts focused on identity and existential questions.
For low Action Orientation: Co-create small behavioral experiments with clear metrics and accountability.
For low Openness to Psychological Work: Start with psychoeducation on how psychology applies to business success.
reporting.re_test: Re-administer after 3-6 months of coaching to assess shifts in pattern recognition, fear engagement, and action orientation.

draft.claim_boundary: This framework is inferred solely from the public website capture. It reflects the creator's stated focus on psychological bottlenecks, fear, identity, and self-actualization. It does not verify actual client outcomes or the effectiveness of the creator's methods. All dimensions are hypotheses for the creator to calibrate against their own experience.
missing_evidence: No detailed curriculum or methodology for the coaching programs.
No specific behavioral indicators from the creator's own assessment tools.
No data on typical client profiles or baseline scores.
No evidence of how the creator distinguishes between levels of readiness.
No information on the creator's preferred assessment formats (e.g., interviews, questionnaires).

draft.title: Inner-Game Decision and Action Review
draft.question: When fear, uncertainty, self-doubt, perfectionism, or overthinking appears in work, how effectively does the respondent identify the pattern, choose a useful response, and take an appropriately bounded action?

dimensions.name: Fear response and approach behavior
dimensions.note: Hypothesis: the creator may value treating fear as information or a catalyst rather than as an automatic reason to stop.
observable_manifestations: Names the specific situation and feared consequence before deciding what to do
Distinguishes a meaningful risk from an avoidance response
Takes a bounded action while fear or uncertainty remains present
Reviews what happened without treating discomfort alone as evidence of failure
evidence: transform your relationship with fear so it becomes a catalyst for growth instead of an obstacle
The Four Horsemen of Fear
the fears that prevent us from publishing and iterating

dimensions.name: Action despite procrastination and overthinking
dimensions.note: Hypothesis: the creator may assess whether respondents convert ambitious intentions into observable next steps rather than waiting for certainty.
observable_manifestations: Identifies the next publishable, testable, or otherwise observable step
Sets a decision or action boundary instead of continuing open-ended analysis
Produces or tests a draft before it feels fully complete
Uses the result to select a next iteration
evidence: The Action Gap
even the most ambitious people struggle to achieve what they’re capable of
the fears that prevent us from publishing and iterating
perfectionism, overthinking

dimensions.name: Interpretation of self-doubt and imposter experiences
dimensions.note: Hypothesis: the creator may encourage interpreting imposter feelings as possible evidence of transition or challenge, not as a definitive verdict about capability.
observable_manifestations: Separates the feeling of not belonging from specific evidence about performance
States what new responsibility, role, or uncertainty is being encountered
Seeks relevant feedback or evidence rather than relying only on self-judgment
Continues, adapts, or deliberately declines based on evidence and values
evidence: What if Imposter Syndrome wasn’t a sign to back off, but actually a good sign?
Liminal Tension
constant self-doubt

dimensions.name: Pattern recognition and underlying choice
dimensions.note: Hypothesis: the creator may value moving from a surface business question to the recurring pattern or choice shaping the respondent’s behavior.
observable_manifestations: Describes a repeated situation using concrete decisions and consequences
Identifies a possible recurring pattern without presenting it as proven fact
Connects the pattern to a current choice or behavior that can be changed
Chooses an experiment or conversation that could provide disconfirming evidence
evidence: get underneath the surface problem to the real one
understanding the pattern in me that created it
what’s holding you back, what you actually want, and how to achieve it

dimensions.name: Alignment between stated aims and action
dimensions.note: Hypothesis: the creator may assess whether respondents clarify what they actually want and make decisions consistent with that aim.
observable_manifestations: States the desired outcome in behavioral or decision terms
Identifies a conflict between the stated aim and the current pattern
Explains what trade-off they are willing to accept
Takes or schedules a specific action consistent with the clarified aim
evidence: what you actually want
Giving Yourself Permission to Choose Your Own Path
Self-actualization
Evolution is a requirement for success

questions.text: Describe a recent work situation in which fear or uncertainty affected whether you published, shipped, asked, or decided. What did you fear, what evidence did you have, and what bounded action did you take?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the respondent can distinguish fear from evidence and act without requiring fear to disappear.
questions.behavior_being_tested: Concrete identification of a feared consequence, evidence review, and follow-through on a bounded action.
questions.scoring_logic: Score higher when the response names a specific situation, separates feeling from evidence, chooses a proportionate action, and reports what was learned. Score lower when it remains abstract or treats fear alone as a stop signal.
questions.strong_signal: A specific publishing or decision example with a stated risk, a limited experiment, and a review of the result.
questions.weak_signal: General claims about being brave or confident without a concrete decision or action.
confounders: The situation may involve genuinely high external risk.
Access to resources, authority, or feedback may constrain available actions.
source_basis: transform your relationship with fear so it becomes a catalyst for growth instead of an obstacle
the fears that prevent us from publishing and iterating

questions.text: You have a strong idea but have revised it repeatedly for three weeks. A smaller version could be shared tomorrow, but it may receive criticism. What would you do over the next 48 hours, and what would count as useful information?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the respondent can interrupt overthinking and use a small release or test to create information.
questions.behavior_being_tested: Selecting a minimum viable action, setting a time boundary, and defining an evidence-based review.
questions.scoring_logic: Score higher when the response specifies what will be shared, when, what feedback matters, and how it will inform iteration. Score lower when it adds indefinite preparation or uses anticipated criticism as the sole decision rule.
questions.strong_signal: A time-bounded draft or test with explicit learning criteria and a planned iteration.
questions.weak_signal: Either immediate abandonment or continued revision without a release condition.
confounders: Some work requires quality, safety, legal, or confidentiality review.
The respondent may lack permission or access to publish the material.
source_basis: The Action Gap
the fears that prevent us from publishing and iterating
perfectionism, overthinking

questions.text: A new role or opportunity makes you feel that you do not belong. What specific evidence would you examine before deciding to proceed, adapt, seek support, or decline?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the respondent treats self-doubt as a signal to investigate rather than a conclusive judgment.
questions.behavior_being_tested: Separating internal experience from external evidence and making a deliberate decision.
questions.scoring_logic: Score higher when the response identifies concrete capability requirements, feedback sources, and a decision threshold. Score lower when it equates discomfort with incompetence or dismisses all concerns as irrational.
questions.strong_signal: A balanced plan to gather relevant evidence while taking a reversible next step or making an explicit decision.
questions.weak_signal: A personality-based conclusion such as 'I am an impostor' or 'feelings never matter.'
confounders: The respondent may face discrimination, exclusion, or an objectively unsuitable opportunity.
Self-report may not accurately represent actual performance.
source_basis: What if Imposter Syndrome wasn’t a sign to back off, but actually a good sign?
Liminal Tension

questions.text: Choose a recurring work problem you have described as a productivity, business, or decision issue. What pattern in your own choices might be contributing, what evidence supports that hypothesis, and what would you test next?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the respondent can move from a surface description to a testable behavioral hypothesis without overclaiming causality.
questions.behavior_being_tested: Reviewing repeated situations, identifying one's own behavior, and designing a falsifiable experiment.
questions.scoring_logic: Score higher when the response cites multiple concrete instances, labels the explanation as a hypothesis, and proposes a test. Score lower when it blames a fixed trait or asserts an untested hidden cause.
questions.strong_signal: A specific recurring behavior, supporting examples, uncertainty about the interpretation, and a next experiment.
questions.weak_signal: A vague label such as 'I self-sabotage' with no observable examples or test.
confounders: External constraints may explain much of the recurring problem.
A short review period may not reveal a stable pattern.
source_basis: get underneath the surface problem to the real one
understanding the pattern in me that created it

questions.text: State one outcome you want in the next month, the current action that conflicts with it, the trade-off you are willing to accept, and the next action you will schedule.
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the respondent can translate a personally meaningful aim into a coherent choice and scheduled behavior.
questions.behavior_being_tested: Clarifying an aim, identifying an inconsistency, acknowledging trade-offs, and committing to a concrete action.
questions.scoring_logic: Score higher when the aim is specific, the conflict is observable, the trade-off is explicit, and the action has a time or completion condition. Score lower when the aim is abstract or the action depends on feeling ready.
questions.strong_signal: A clear near-term outcome paired with a scheduled, observable action and an acknowledged cost.
questions.weak_signal: A broad aspiration with no changed behavior, trade-off, or timing.
confounders: The respondent may not control the stated outcome.
Short-term actions may not capture longer-term values or constraints.
source_basis: what you actually want, and how to achieve it
Giving Yourself Permission to Choose Your Own Path

fields: Dimension-level evidence cited by the respondent
recommended_interventions: Define a smaller, time-bounded action and a review criterion.
Separate feared outcomes from evidence and identify a proportionate experiment.
Collect relevant feedback before making a global judgment about capability or belonging.
Map repeated situations and label explanations as hypotheses to test.
Clarify the desired outcome, acceptable trade-off, and next scheduled behavior.
reporting.re_test: Re-administer with a new concrete situation after an agreed interval, comparing the specificity of evidence, action taken, feedback gathered, and iteration. Do not interpret change as proof of a stable personal trait or causal effect.

draft.claim_boundary: This is a hypothesis about an assessment for the creator's founders, leaders, and creators audience. It evaluates reported or scenario-based behaviors and judgments, not psychological diagnoses, stable traits, business growth, or the effectiveness of the creator's methods. Terms such as fear, imposter experiences, and underlying patterns are retained from the source as topic labels, not clinical conclusions.
missing_evidence: No source-defined rubric, scoring scale, pass threshold, or weighting is provided.
No operational definitions are provided for 'Four Horsemen of Fear,' 'psychological bottlenecks,' 'self-actualization,' or 'success.'
No source evidence specifies the intended time horizon, acceptable risk level, or required behavioral standard.
No source evidence establishes that the proposed behaviors cause business growth or other outcomes.
No source evidence indicates whether the assessment should be self-administered, coached, observed, or based on work artifacts.

draft.title: Hypothesis Framework: Inner-Game Bottleneck Self-Assessment for Founders, Leaders, and Creators (Draft for Creator Calibration)
draft.question: Based on the captured site, which observable decisions and situations in a founder's, leader's, or creator's work suggest that a psychological bottleneck (fear, self-doubt, procrastination, or perfectionism) is limiting progress, and how might the creator help the audience notice and act on those patterns? (Hypothesis only; the creator must confirm the framework matches their actual teaching.)

dimensions.name: Fear-driven avoidance of visible output
dimensions.note: Hypothesis derived from the site's framing of fear as an obstacle and the 'Four Horsemen of Fear' and publishing-related testimonial. Tests whether the respondent avoids shipping, publishing, or iterating in public.
observable_manifestations: Delays publishing or releasing work after it is 'ready enough'
Repeatedly revises a piece instead of shipping it
Declines speaking, posting, or pitching opportunities that carry visibility
Abandons projects before feedback is collected
evidence: "Learn how to transform your relationship with fear so it becomes a catalyst for growth instead of an obstacle holding you back."
"he goes deeper into understanding the fears that prevent us from publishing and iterating."

dimensions.name: Self-doubt and imposter-related interpretation
dimensions.note: Hypothesis based on the site's emphasis on Imposter Syndrome and 'Liminal Tension' as a reframe. Tests how the respondent interprets self-doubt when it arises, not whether they 'have' Imposter Syndrome.
observable_manifestations: Responds to self-doubt by pausing or withdrawing from a decision
Responds to self-doubt by seeking more reassurance before acting
Describes a recent doubt and whether it changed the next action
Reframes discomfort as a signal to stop versus a signal of transition
evidence: "What if Imposter Syndrome wasn't a sign to back off, but actually a good sign?"
"Say goodbye to procrastination, Imposter Syndrome, perfectionism, overthinking, constant self-doubt"

dimensions.name: Procrastination and perfectionism in task initiation
dimensions.note: Hypothesis from the site's named target behaviors. Scenario-based; tests specific task-start and completion decisions.
observable_manifestations: Postpones high-stakes tasks until deadlines force action
Keeps refining drafts past the point of diminishing returns
Sets standards that prevent completion of minimum viable outputs
Overthinks options before committing to one
evidence: "Say goodbye to procrastination, Imposter Syndrome, perfectionism, overthinking"
"Why Ambitious People Sabotage Their Success"

dimensions.name: Surface problem versus underlying pattern
dimensions.note: Hypothesis from testimonial language about getting 'underneath the surface problem.' Tests whether the respondent attributes stalled outcomes to external factors or examines recurring personal patterns. Interpretive; the site does not show a method for this.
observable_manifestations: Attributes a stalled project to tools, time, or market without examining repeated behavior
Can name a recurring pattern across two or more unrelated business decisions
Revisits past decisions to identify what drove them
Asks for a second opinion on the 'real' problem before acting
evidence: "get underneath the surface problem to the real one"
"I'd come in with a business question and leave understanding the pattern in me that created it."

dimensions.name: Identity and values alignment in goals
dimensions.note: Hypothesis from the site's references to 'what you actually want,' identity-level work, and self-actualization. Tests whether stated goals are tied to choices the respondent actually makes. Requires creator definition of 'identity-level.'
observable_manifestations: Pursues goals that others expect rather than goals the respondent describes as their own
Makes a stated priority inconsistent with calendar or spending
Can describe what success would look like in their own terms
Changes a goal after noticing a mismatch with values
evidence: "what you actually want, and how to achieve it"
"A non-hyperbolic, psychology-based understanding of what holds us back from self-actualization"

dimensions.name: Willingness to change behavior in response to insight
dimensions.note: Hypothesis from the site's 'Evolution is a requirement' and action-focused framing. Tests whether insight translates into a changed action within a defined window.
observable_manifestations: Selects one concrete behavior change after a reflection exercise
Reports completing the change within a set period
Reverts to prior behavior under stress and notes the reversion
Seeks feedback on whether the change held
evidence: "Evolution is a requirement for success if you want to change your life."
"The Action Gap: 9 reasons even the most ambitious people struggle to achieve what they're capable of"

questions.text: Think of a piece of work (post, product, pitch, or talk) that you have not yet released. What is the main reason it is still unreleased, and what would have to be true for you to release it this week?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the stated reason for delay is a concrete external constraint or a recurring internal hold-back.
questions.behavior_being_tested: Release or non-release of a specific artifact and the reasoning given.
questions.scoring_logic: Score 1 if the reason is a specific external constraint with a dated next step; 2 if the reason is 'not ready' with no defined readiness criterion; 3 if the respondent names a fear or self-judgment and a counter-action.
questions.strong_signal: Names a concrete readiness criterion and a dated action, or names a specific fear and tests it with a small release.
questions.weak_signal: Vague readiness language with no date or criterion, repeated across several items.
confounders: Quality standards appropriate to the domain
source_basis: "the fears that prevent us from publishing and iterating"

questions.text: Describe the last time self-doubt showed up before a business decision. What did you do next, and what did you do afterward?
questions.what_it_tests: The observable sequence of action after self-doubt, not the presence of doubt.
questions.behavior_being_tested: Action taken after a doubt-triggered moment.
questions.scoring_logic: Score by whether the respondent proceeded, paused with a defined check, or withdrew indefinitely; note whether the outcome was reviewed.
questions.strong_signal: Doubt noted, a specific check run, decision made, and outcome reviewed.
questions.weak_signal: Decision deferred without a check or review date, or doubt used as the sole reason not to act.
source_basis: "Imposter Syndrome wasn't a sign to back off"

questions.text: List three tasks you postponed this month. For each, write the time you first intended to start and the actual start, plus one thing you were doing instead.
questions.what_it_tests: Whether postponement is clustered by task type (e.g., high-visibility or evaluative tasks).
questions.scoring_logic: Count delay length and whether delayed tasks share an evaluative or visibility feature; code as clustered or scattered.
questions.strong_signal: Delays concentrate on tasks where feedback or judgment is expected.
questions.weak_signal: Delays are scattered with no shared feature, or the log is incomplete.
confounders: Recall bias if not logged in real time
source_basis: "Say goodbye to procrastination"

questions.text: Pick one stalled project. Write the surface explanation you would give a colleague, then list the last three decisions you made about it and what they have in common.
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the respondent can move from a surface cause to a recurring decision pattern.
questions.behavior_being_tested: Gap between stated explanation and documented decision history.
questions.scoring_logic: Score 1 if the pattern list is absent; 2 if decisions are listed without a shared theme; 3 if a recurring decision theme is named and tied to a specific behavior.
questions.strong_signal: Names a recurring decision theme that differs from the surface explanation and proposes a test.
questions.weak_signal: Surface explanation is repeated with no decision-level evidence.
source_basis: "get underneath the surface problem to the real one"

questions.text: Which goal on your current list would you keep if no one else would ever see the result? What share of your last two weeks went to it?
questions.what_it_tests: Consistency between stated goals and time allocation.
questions.behavior_being_tested: Stated priority versus recorded time use.
questions.scoring_logic: Compare the chosen goal to time log; score alignment as high, partial, or absent.
questions.strong_signal: Chosen goal receives a proportionate share of recorded time.
questions.weak_signal: Chosen goal receives little or no time while other goals dominate, with no stated reason.
source_basis: "what you actually want, and how to achieve it"

questions.text: Choose one behavior change you committed to in the last month. Did you complete it, what got in the way, and what did you change in response?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether reflection produces a completed, reviewed behavior change.
questions.behavior_being_tested: Completion and adjustment of a specific committed change.
questions.scoring_logic: Score completion (yes/partial/no) and whether an adjustment followed a failure; high if completed or adjusted with a stated next step.
questions.strong_signal: Completed or adapted change with a specific obstacle named and addressed.
questions.weak_signal: No commitment recorded, or obstacle named without any adjustment.
confounders: Unusually high or low workload month
source_basis: "Evolution is a requirement for success if you want to change your life."

fields: Question-level scores with the scoring logic applied
Confidence rating per dimension and reason for any MISSING
Items where external constraints plausibly explain the pattern
recommended_interventions: Creator defines what 'psychological bottleneck' means operationally before scoring
Creator supplies their actual framework (e.g., Four Horsemen of Fear, Liminal Tension) so dimensions map to taught concepts rather than inferred ones
Pair each scored pattern with a small, dated behavior test rather than an interpretive label
Separate external-constraint explanations from internal-pattern explanations in every report
Review reports with the respondent before any conclusion is stated
reporting.re_test: Repeat the scenario and artifact items after a defined interval (e.g., 6 to 8 weeks) using the same prompts, and compare documented actions rather than self-rated insight.

draft.claim_boundary: This is a hypothesis for creator calibration built only from one bounded public homepage capture. It shows the creator's named topics (fear, imposter syndrome, procrastination, perfectionism, surface vs. underlying problems, goals, action) and testimonial language, but it does not show the creator's actual assessment method, scoring rules, validation, outcomes, or the audience's characteristics. Testimonials are quoted as presented and not treated as evidence of effect. No diagnosis, personality trait, or causal claim is supported. Dimensions and questions are interpretations requiring creator review.
missing_evidence: Creator's actual framework definitions (Four Horsemen of Fear, Liminal Tension, Action Gap) and their components
Any scoring, rubric, or validation method used by the creator
Intended audience sub-segments and their stated goals
Content of the Masterclass, Inner Game Intensive, or Alchemy of Fear Program beyond homepage summaries
Evidence of how the creator defines 'psychological bottleneck' or 'identity-level' work operationally
Any outcome data, follow-up, or re-test evidence
Ethical or scope boundaries for non-clinical coaching (the capture describes the work as coaching; clinical boundaries are MISSING)
